subtype: Feeling anonymous in a large team [Actor]
passage: Wednesday. Our hackathon team has thirty-two people and I have been doing very little. Nobody knows who wrote what in the shared file, and everything goes under "Team 7". I skipped the last two calls and nobody messaged. Sabina, the coordinator, said "great work, everyone" and I felt nothing. It made me think of last term, when I did the whole marine-life slide for a small group. Everyone praised that one, and I stayed up till two. So maybe it is not laziness, more that this feels like shouting into a big hall. Tomorrow I will ask Sabina whether I can take one named part. — Rehana

qa.q: How many people are on the hackathon team?
qa.a: The hackathon team has thirty-two people.

qa.q: Why does Rehana feel nothing when Sabina says "great work, everyone"?
qa.a: Rehana feels anonymous and unseen, as if the effort cannot be traced or would not matter; the praise is for everyone, so it does not reach anyone.

qa.q: What choice does Rehana make at the end of the entry?
qa.a: Rehana decides to ask Sabina for one named part, so the work is visible, as it was when Rehana did the marine-life slide.

qa.q: What might Sabina, as coordinator of thirty-two people, be seeing about Rehana's calls?
qa.a: Sabina may not have noticed the skipped calls among so many people, which shows how easily one person's absence goes unseen in a big team.

grounding: A student in a big group feels their contribution cannot be traced, so effort drops, though the same student works hard when their part is visible.
